key_insight: Data-driven equation discovery can recover liquid-film flow dynamics, but even in a best-case setting it is limited by multicollinearity and difficult early-time transients.
engineering_relevance: The study clarifies when equation-discovery methods can support reduced-order modeling and physics inference for nonlinear film flows used in coating, heat transfer, and surface-flow applications.
method: Curate expert-informed data for a liquid-film flow system with known asymptotic structure.
Use equation discovery to identify governing PDE terms from a monomial basis library.
Test identifiability under multi-scale dynamics and early transient behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a best-case evaluation with carefully curated data, yet still finds residual-driven training errors and strong identifiability issues from multicollinearity.
watch_item: Monomial basis choices and early-time transient data can make the discovered equations unstable or non-unique, so basis design and regularization are critical.
paper_title: Data-Driven Equation Discovery for Nonlinear Liquid Film Flows
